page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2693.38 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21558.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9379.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1018.3 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 75.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported via hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and AVX.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-16 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data caching. However, its high-density compute allocation makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, web serving, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its 904.0 tokens per second prompt processing speed on small language models.
